record.title: Malaba truck blockade over COVID testing charges in January 2022
record.scope: Kenya-to-Uganda truck approach and crossing at Malaba
record.direction: Kenya to Uganda; broader bilateral closure not established.
record.movement: Uganda-bound trucks and cargo, including fuel; passenger prohibition not established.
record.exceptions: Reverse-direction trucks and Busia flows were reported operating in the early phase.
record.imposing_authority: Protesting truck drivers; associations and union positions differed
record.enforcement: Trucks parked to seal the border approach.
record.consequences: Long queues persisted after traffic resumed; backlog is not continued closure.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no present closure is inferred.
record.official_rationale: Drivers opposed repeat paid COVID testing. No six-code rationale neatly describes this fee protest; Public health is context, not the blockade’s protective purpose.
record.context: Road sealing accompanied the drivers’ refusal to proceed. A 10 January regional agreement changed testing arrangements.
record.uncertainty: Sources date onset to 1 or 3 January. Call-off and continuation reports conflict on 11 January. The endpoint is passage confirmed by 20 January, not the first reopening date.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. Month onset, contested ending chronology and residual queues preclude an exact duration. Actual reopening labels observed passage within the recorded scope; the date is confirmation by that day, not a proven first resumption or durable end.
